To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the molecular characteristics of pectic constituents in relation to firmness, extractable juice, and wooliness in nectarines were studied.
extractable juice, firmness, and woolly nectarines are related to the molecular characteristics of soluble pectin.

the differences in extractable juices, woolly fruit, and composition and gelling properties of soluble pectic substances between cold-stored and noncold-stored nectarines are related to molecular characteristics of the pectic constituents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular properties of soluble pectin in nectarines and their relationship with extractable juice, firmness, and wooliness.
the molecular characteristics of pectins in nectarines in relation to fruit firmness, extractable juice, and woolly fruit formation.
the molecular characteristics of soluble pectic constituents and their relationship to fruit quality attributes during ripening of nectarines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular characteristics of pectins in relation to extractable juice and woolliness are dependent on the ripening stage and the previous cold storage treatment.
the extractable juice is inversely proportional to the viscosity of soluble and insoluble pectins.
the extractable juice is a good indicator of the firmness of nectarines and that the extractable pectin content is not a reliable indicator of the degree of firmness of the fruit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the differences in extractable juiceness, woolly- ness, and composition of extracted pectin between cold- and noncold-stored nectarines during ripening were related to differences in the molecular mass distribution of the pectic constituents in the cell walls.

as fruit softens during ripening the extractable juice increases, but the soluble pectic constituents become more viscous and less effective as gelling agents, resulting in a decrease in the gel strength.
the extractable juice, pectin composition, and gell- ing characteristics of soluble pectin are related to fruit firmness and woolly breakdown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the changes in pectin characteristics during ripening are different when fruit has been subjected to cold storage compared to when it has not.
the extractable juice is not a good indicator of fruit firmness.
extractable juice, firmness, and pectin characteristics are closely related to woolly fruit formation in nectarines.
